# Linux BashBound

> An interactive Linux and Unix learning platform: a 16-level roadmap, 40 modules, 128 documented commands, 1282 interview questions, a simulated shell, quizzes and incident labs. Static site, no account, progress stored in the browser.

## Start here

- [Roadmap](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): the 16 levels in dependency order
- [All modules](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn): the full curriculum index
- [Command explorer](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/commands): 128 commands with syntax, flags and examples
- [Interview arena](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/interview): 1282 questions with answers and explanations
- [Terminal sandbox](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/terminal): a simulated shell; nothing runs on the host

## Curriculum

- [Level 00 — Linux Fundamentals](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Operating systems, distributions, kernel vs user space, boot, and the filesystem map.
- [Level 01 — Terminal & Shell](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Terminal vs shell, prompts, arguments, PATH, quoting, history, and expansion.
- [Level 02 — Filesystem](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Inodes, links, descriptors, mount points, and the FHS directories you will live in.
- [Level 03 — Users & Permissions](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Users, groups, sudo, mode bits, umask, special bits, and ACLs.
- [Level 04 — Processes](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): PID, fork/exec, jobs, signals, priorities, zombies, and daemons.
- [Level 05 — Networking](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): IP, TCP/UDP, DNS, routing, SSH, and the commands you will use daily.
- [Level 06 — Package Management](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): APT, DNF, Pacman, RPM/DEB, repositories, and dependencies.
- [Level 07 — Bash Scripting](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Variables, control flow, pipes, redirection, functions, and production scripts.
- [Level 08 — System Administration](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): systemd, logs, timers, SSH configuration, hostname, and locale.
- [Level 09 — Storage & Filesystems](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): GPT/MBR, ext4/XFS/Btrfs, LVM, fstab, and capacity tools.
- [Level 10 — Security](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): SSH keys, firewalls, SELinux/AppArmor, audit, and hardening.
- [Level 11 — Performance & Monitoring](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Load average, memory, I/O, caching, swap, and the standard toolkit.
- [Level 12 — Networking Internals](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): TCP handshake, sockets, routing lookups, and packet path on Linux.
- [Level 13 — Advanced Linux](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, virtual memory, IPC, epoll.
- [Level 14 — Unix & POSIX](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): Unix history, POSIX, BSD vs System V, and how macOS fits.
- [Level 15 — Production Linux](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/roadmap): DevOps-facing Linux: services, observability, incidents, and change control.

## Modules

- [What is Linux?](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/what-is-linux): Linux is a kernel, and a Linux system is that kernel plus userland tools, libraries, and a package-managed distribution.
- [Linux vs Unix](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/linux-vs-unix): Unix is a family of operating systems and a design culture. Linux is a Unix-like kernel that is not derived from AT&T Unix source.
- [Linux distributions](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/distributions): Pick a distro family and you pick a package format, release model, and default administration style.
- [Kernel, GNU, and open source](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/kernel-and-gnu): A typical Linux system is GNU userland plus the Linux kernel, licensed as free and open source software.
- [Linux architecture](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/architecture): Applications talk to the kernel through system calls. The kernel talks to hardware. The shell is just another user program.
- [Boot process and init](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/boot-and-init): Firmware loads a bootloader, the bootloader loads the kernel, the kernel starts PID 1 (usually systemd).
- [Directory structure (FHS)](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/directory-map): Linux paths are a contract: /etc is config, /var is variable data, /usr is shipped software, /home is people.
- [man, info, and --help](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/help-systems): The local system documents itself. Learn the sections and you become independent.
- [Terminal, console, and shell](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/terminal-shell): The terminal displays bytes. The shell interprets your typing. They are not the same program.
- [Bash commands, arguments, and the prompt](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/bash-basics): A command line is a program name plus arguments. The prompt is a hint, not part of the command.
- [Environment variables and PATH](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/env-and-path): Child processes inherit environment variables. PATH is the list of directories searched for commands.
- [Quoting, escaping, and expansion](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/quoting-expansion): The shell rewrites your line before the program sees it: globs, variables, command substitution, word splitting.
- [Inodes, hard links, and symbolic links](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/inodes-and-links): A filename is a directory entry pointing at an inode. Hard links are extra names. Symlinks are path strings.
- [Mounts and mount points](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/mounts): A filesystem is usable only after it is mounted on a directory.
- [Important directories in depth](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/fhs-deep-dive): /etc configuration, /var state, /usr shipped software, /proc and /sys kernel interfaces, /dev devices, /run runtime.
- [Users, groups, root, and sudo](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/users-groups): Identity is a UID and GIDs. Root is UID 0. sudo is controlled delegation.
- [Permission bits, chmod, chown, umask](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/mode-bits): Each file has owner, group, and a mode: rwx for user, group, others.
- [setuid, setgid, sticky bit, and ACLs](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/special-bits-acl): Special mode bits change execution identity or deletion rules. ACLs add named users beyond owner/group/other.
- [What is a process?](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/process-model): A process is a running program with a PID, memory, file descriptors, and credentials.
- [Jobs, foreground, background, signals](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/jobs-signals): Job control is a shell feature. Signals are kernel messages to processes.
- [Monitoring and controlling processes](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/process-control): ps, top, nice, and zombie/orphan behavior.
- [IP, TCP, UDP, and ports](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/net-fundamentals): Hosts have addresses. Processes bind ports. TCP is a connection; UDP is datagrams.
- [DNS, DHCP, and routing basics](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/name-resolution): DHCP configures an address. DNS maps names. Routing decides the next hop.
- [SSH and copying files](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/remote-access): SSH is the standard encrypted admin channel. Keys beat passwords.
- [Package management](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/package-managers): Packages are signed bundles with metadata and dependencies, served from repositories.
- [Bash scripting fundamentals](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/bash-scripting): Variables, tests, loops, functions, exit codes, and set -euo pipefail with its caveats.
- [Pipes, redirection, and descriptors](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/pipes-redirection): stdin 0, stdout 1, stderr 2. Pipes connect stdout of one process to stdin of the next.
- [Practical Bash scripts](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/practical-scripts): Backup, log grep, disk check, service check, file organizer — patterns you can adapt.
- [systemd units and services](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/systemd): Units describe services, sockets, mounts, timers. systemctl is the control plane.
- [Logs, cron, and timers](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/logs-and-jobs): journald is the systemd log. cron and systemd timers schedule work.
- [Hostname, time, locale, SSH server](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/host-config): Identity of a machine: name, clock, language, and how admins log in.
- [Disks, partitions, and filesystem types](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/disks-partitions): Block devices are split into partitions with a table (GPT or MBR) and formatted with a filesystem.
- [LVM, fstab, df, and du](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/lvm-and-fstab): LVM abstracts disks into flexible volumes. fstab mounts them at boot. df vs du diagnose fullness.
- [Linux security model](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/linux-security): Discretionary permissions, sudo, SSH, MAC (SELinux/AppArmor), firewalls, and least privilege.
- [Performance and monitoring](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/performance-basics): Measure CPU, memory, disk, network before changing anything. Load average is a queue length.
- [TCP internals and Linux sockets](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/tcp-and-sockets): Handshake, states, and how Linux represents connections as inodes/sockets.
- [Namespaces, cgroups, and containers](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/namespaces-cgroups): Containers are processes with isolated namespaces and limited cgroups — not a second kernel.
- [Virtual memory and IPC](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/memory-ipc): Each process has a virtual address space. The kernel maps pages. Processes talk via pipes, sockets, shm, signals.
- [Unix history, POSIX, BSD, and macOS](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/unix-posix): POSIX is the portable contract. BSD and System V are historic Unix branches. macOS is Unix-certified with a BSD userland and a Mach/XNU kernel.
- [Production Linux and DevOps practice](https://vivekkumarq.github.io/linux-bashbound/learn/production-linux): Production means change control, observability, backups, least privilege, and reversible deploys.
